## Representative excerpts

### Philoctetes: Section 6

_Dialogue and character voice_

> Enter Odysseus, Neoptolemus; in the background, a Sailor. Odysseus Son of Achilles, Neoptolemus, Sprung from the noblest of the Grecian host, This is the beach of Lemnos, sea-girt isle, A land untrod, untenanted, where once, As bidden by the chiefs, I put ashore The Malian, son of Poeas, grievously Afflicted by his foot’s envenomed wound. For us there was no peace at sacrifice Or at libations, but the whole camp rang With his discordant screams and savage yells, Moaning and groaning. But what skills it now To tell this tale? No time for large discourse That might betray our presence and undo The plot I’ve laid to catch him presently. To work!
